correctness.rationale: False-twin necessity is invariant throughout the forcing process: with two white false twins no neighbor can force either first. Under the no-singleton hypothesis every class contains a blue witness, and the canonical staircase neighborhoods give a valid forward B-class pass followed by a reverse A-class pass. This proves the exact set characterization. Multiplying the two allowable choices for each class yields the polynomial. A standalone exhaustive checker independently verified 60 weighted canonical chain graphs and 128,016 subsets through order twelve and checked the singleton boundary on P4.

originality.rationale: The accepted statement is the exact zero-forcing-set characterization and polynomial factorization on chain graphs with no singleton canonical twin class. Targeted statement-level searches across principal aliases and accessible full-text comparison with the zero-forcing-polynomial paper found no equivalent or stronger claim. value.rationale: The no-singleton-twin condition defines an infinite, natural blow-up regime of chain graphs where the inevitable false-twin lower bound becomes exactly sufficient. The theorem determines all zero forcing sets, not merely Z(G), and factors the full polynomial, yielding minimum-set counts and root structure immediately. Singleton classes genuinely break the simple criterion, as P4 demonstrates, so the boundary has mathematical content rather than being an arbitrary finite slice.
